meant.why: A meeting's file is an Attachment, and its drawer's fact naming it says so too; the fact is never a row.
Attachments steps in to a meeting's or a mail's files, and its drawer's fact naming several says so too; the fact is never a row.
A manager kept out by its setting can't be locked as well, so only one of the two leads Passwords for it at a time, each by the manager's name.
Both list devices: sound's outputs and inputs, and what's paired.
The terminal, Neovim and the browser all have tabs, and each group says what holds it beside it.
The terminal, Neovim and the browser all go to a tab by its number, and each group says what holds it beside it.
GIMP and Inkscape both choose a tool by a letter, and each group says which program's it is beside it.
GIMP and the reader both select, and each group says which program's it is beside it.
The reader and the PDF viewer both scroll a page, and each group says which program's it is beside it.
Neovim and the reader both take keys on their command line, and each group says which program's it is beside it.
Focus goes to a window, a column, a workspace or a screen alike, and each group says what holds it beside it.
A window and a column each move where they sit, and each group says what holds it beside it.
A column moves to another workspace or another screen, and each group says what holds it beside it.
A window moves to another workspace or another screen, and each group says what holds it beside it.
The terminal sizes its text and Neovim searches it, and each group says what holds it beside it.
The terminal and pi each scroll back through what they showed, and each group says what holds it beside it.
Inside the stopwatch, Lap marks one and each lap it marked is named by its number, so lap finds the act and the laps together.
The video player's drawer and the reader's each say what was left part way, and each is said only in its own program's drawer.

usage: Shows a place or a row the launcher holds, its drawer and what is inside it,
as the launcher would: launcher show machine disk. Each step is a row's name,
in any case, a hyphen for a space, or the start of only one. With none, it
shows home. --drawers shows every row's drawer after the rows. --json prints
what the launcher says as JSON, with every row's drawer given --drawers.
After --, every word is a step, so one starting with a hyphen can be named.
launcher do does what a row does on Return, and any act a place offers among
its rows, as : offers it: launcher do programs kitty. One that ends something
asks first, as the launcher does, and with no terminal to answer on it's done
only with --yes. Words an act asks for follow --. A place opens in the
launcher completion zsh writes zsh's completion, which offers each place's
